title: Assign token-level billing provenance for hybrid prefix/KV-cache + fused-batch flows
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe inconsistent billing and quota accounting for requests that are partially served by prefix/KV caches and then merged into fused/aggregated batches. Mixed provenance within a batch causes two classes of errors: (1) double-counting when cached tokens are treated as generated in downstream metering, and (2) under-charging when generation tokens for one request are attributed to another request in coalesced batches. These errors are visible in Finance reconciliations and in customer quota complaints (unexpected usage spikes).

Goal: Produce a deterministic, auditable way to attribute per-token cost/quotas based on token provenance (generated vs served-from-cache vs prefetch) across fused batch execution paths, while keeping runtime overhead low and preserving latency SLOs.

Constraints and requirements:
- Must not materially increase p99 latency for hot paths (target < 1% added overhead).
- Must produce meterable events that allow offline reconciliation and real-time quota enforcement.
- Backwards-compatible with existing billing pipeline (can emit legacy-compatible aggregate counters if needed).
- Support multi-tenant Dedicated and Private deployments with tenant isolation for chargeback.

Proposed solution (chosen): Token Provenance Ledger + Post-process Aggregator
1) Runtime: annotate each request with a compact provenance vector summarizing token ranges and provenance tags (e.g. "0-23:cache-prefix,24-199:generated,200-240:kv-hit"). For fused batches that coalesce multiple requests, preserve per-request provenance and attach a batch_agg_id. This is a small metadata annotation (O(bytes) per request).
2) Metering emitter: extend existing meter events to include three numeric fields emitted per request as strings: "tokens_generated", "tokens_cache_served", "tokens_prefetch" plus "batch_agg_id" and "provenance_digest" (digest is a stable compact string of the vector). The ingestion layer will trust the runtime-provided token counts for attribution.
3) Ingestion/aggregator: at meter ingestion, expand digest into tokens by provenance and attribute billing units: full unit charge for tokens_generated; configurable micro-charge (or zero) for tokens_cache_served and tokens_prefetch based on customer pricing plan. Aggregator will detect mismatches between runtime token counts and per-batch totals and emit reconciliation alerts.
4) Fallback heuristic: for older runtimes or traffic where provenance metadata is missing, use a conservative estimation rule (bill as generated) and mark for downstream reconciliation sampling.

Trade-offs considered:
- Alternative A: Ingest per-token streaming provenance (fine-grain but high bandwidth). Rejected due to packet overhead and ingestion cost.
- Alternative B: Heuristic attribution using prefix-hit heuristics at ingestion without runtime metadata. Rejected because it cannot guarantee correctness for fused batches and causes >2% reconciliation drift in benchmarks.

Performance & cost mitigation:
- Provenance metadata is compact; we added a compact encoding to keep per-request overhead < 96 bytes on average.
- For high-throughput tenants we enable sampling (1% of requests carry full provenance vectors) and extrapolate if load becomes an issue; sampling only used as fallback, not default.

Acceptance criteria:
- Production reconciliation delta vs ledgered GPU token accounting < 0.5% after 2 weeks on sampled traffic (target).
- Finance reconciliation alerts reduced by 90% on pilot customers.
- No p99 latency regression beyond 1% on canary fleet.
- Real-time quota enforcement correctly prevents >99.9% of quota breaches observed in the pilot window.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Runtime prototype in canary fleet (internal). Emit provenance metadata and meter events to a safe ingestion topic.
- Week 2: Aggregator consumer reads provenance and produces mapped billing lines to a staging billing table. Run offline reconciliation against GPU execution logs.
- Week 3: Pilot with two high-volume customers (opt-in) in Dedicated. Compare charges and collect feedback.
- Week 4: Expand to 25% of production traffic with sampling enabled. Finance and Billing on-call to monitor.
- Week 6: Full rollout behind runtime feature flag; gradual enable for all customers over two weeks.

- Alerts: reconciliation_delta > 1% sustained for 15m; provenance_missing_rate > 10% for a tenant.

comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after finance reported 3 discrepant customer invoices attributed to cache/generation mismatch.
2026-03-03 - Luca Moretti: Ran microbenchmarks of provenance encoding. Overhead ~45 bytes/request on average; p99 CPU negligible on canary cores.
2026-03-05 - Priya Anand (Billing): Reviewed and requested explicit fields for tokens_prefetch to handle prefetch accounting. Added in design.

2026-03-07 - Miguel Santos (Infra): Flagged that existing kafka topic partitioning requires batch_agg_id stable hashing to allow consumer-side group-by. We proposed including batch_agg_id as a single string field.
2026-03-09 - Finance (Rohan Das): Pilot customers agreed to opt-in for week-3 pilot; requested daily reconciliation dump to validate charges.
2026-03-11 - Luca Moretti: Deployed runtime prototype to canary fleet (internal). Emitting provenance metadata to staging-metering topic. No regressions observed on p50/p95; p99 +0.3%.
2026-03-13 - Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria and set release target runtime-2.4. Blocker: legal needs to confirm pricing table micro-charge for cache-served tokens if nonzero.
Notes: If legal disallows micro-charges for cache tokens, aggregator will map cache-served tokens to zero-cost entries but still include them in ledger for visibility.
